about: Per game. disagreements: PokéAPI vs Serebii species disagreements per area and version, each settled by the game's table on Bulbapedia's location page (source): keep/drop = a PokéAPI row Bulbapedia lists / doesn't list; add/skip = a Serebii-only row Bulbapedia lists / doesn't list; unresolved = no Bulbapedia table, PokéAPI's data stands. bulbapedia: every other wild row Bulbapedia's table doesn't list for that version: drop = Bulbapedia lists the Pokémon there for no version of the game (e.g. an unreleased event table), keep = not on its table (both other sources list it). rates: per Pokémon and method family, PokéAPI's chances (per time slot, summed over the place's parts) that differ from Bulbapedia's table: replace = Serebii's rows (which match Bulbapedia) are used instead; add = PokéAPI lacks the method there and Serebii's matching rows are added; add-bulbapedia = only Bulbapedia has it, its rows are added; keep = no two sources agree, PokéAPI's stand. serebii (Scarlet/Violet, Legends: Z-A, whose Bulbapedia location tables are the source): every Serebii row its place's Bulbapedia table doesn't have; add = the Pokémon's own Bulbapedia page names that place for the game, skip = it doesn't (the row is left out). visible: every row of Bulbapedia's visible-Pokémon sections (Sword/Shield's Visible encounters, Wanderers, Curry encounters), add = no row of the area has that Pokémon met the same way (water or land) at overlapping levels in that version, duplicate = one does (named). coverageLosses: area|species|version(|water or land) keys the merged sources had and the output lost other than by a logged drop; it must be empty (verify:nuzlocke fails otherwise). conditionFixes: PokéAPI condition values found on rows they can't belong to (a Max Raid den value on Rolling Fields' wild rows), with the value used instead and the evidence. fixes: source rows Bulbapedia shows to be wrong and what was done (drop, levels, method, no chance, copied to the places a moving NPC appears at, kind, condition), each with its evidence (scripts/nuzlocke/lib/fixes.ts, Bulbapedia's notes on unreachable water, PokéAPI's Generation VII ambush rows). sweep: the game's Bulbapedia location pages (its category) that no area's lookup reached and that have its table rows: fold = the page is part of an area (a building in a town, by its infobox location; a part, by its title; or a named rule) and joins that area's pages; new area = a place no other source names, built from its page. nonWild: gifts, statics, Eggs and fossils that their area's Bulbapedia pages don't list but another area's do (the same encounter: kind and levels; trades are left where they are): drop = that area already has it, move = it is moved there. unnamedSubs: PokéAPI's unnamed sub-areas ("Unknown area 53") and the part of Bulbapedia's table each was matched to by its encounters (every Pokémon, way, version and level range of it in that part, at least three quarters of the part, and in no other part; parts that all match and share a first name give that name), or null with the reason, its rows then naming no part. battleOnly (Scarlet/Violet, Legends: Arceus, Legends: Z-A): Special encounters boxes left out because the text above them says the Pokémon is only battled (why: the words that say so, e.g. "cannot be caught" or a Rogue Mega Evolution's battle). Written by scripts/nuzlocke/build.ts.

fixes.action: condition "By day it despawns before it can be seen (except in a Union Circle session or as a Shiny); it can be met at night" (5 rows)
fixes.why: Bulbapedia's note on Area Zero's Flutter Mane rows: by day they despawn too fast to be seen unless in a Union Circle session; the quirk spares Shiny ones and the night

fixes.action: condition "After accepting Perrin's request at Blueberry Academy's Terarium (The Indigo Disk), at a specific spot in Area Zero" (4 rows)
fixes.why: Bulbapedia's Area Zero text names all four of these Paradox Pokémon in one sentence; each row (each version's two) needs only what applies to it

fixes.action: condition "During Perrin's hunt for a special Ursaluna in the Timeless Woods (after registering over 150 Pokémon in the Kitakami Pokédex), an Ariados ambushes the player" (2 rows)
fixes.why: the text above the Ariados box opens with the quest and says in its next sentence that an Ariados ambushes the player there; the first sentence alone reads as an Ursaluna note

the walkthrough's "South Province (Area One)" heading opens Part 1 with Cabo Poco inside it; Part 2 goes Poco Path, Inlet Grotto, the Poco Path Lighthouse, then the road through Area One to Los Platos and Mesagoza
